subject: Channel-strip send slots: whether the slot's own menu mark reports the assignment, and what appears once a send is assigned
question: Does anything at the SOURCE report which destination a send slot holds?

reverify.expected: With a send assigned, the slot that owns it still marks the no-send entry: `marked items: 1` and the marked title is the no-send one.

method: The probe gained `--marks`, which reads `AXMenuItemMarkChar` on every item of the opened slot menu, and `--slot-index`, because a strip shows more than one send slot once one is assigned and `first` then answers about whichever the tree orders first. Readings were taken with no send assigned, then after selecting `Bus 12` by title, then after Edit > Undo. The assignment was confirmed from Logic's own undo entry, not from the slot, because the slot's readback is the thing in question.

observations.what: menu marks with no send assigned
observations.title: No Send

observations.what: Logic's undo entry after selecting Bus 12
observations.title: Undo Change Send in Channel Strip

observations.what: a Send Level control in the tree, before the assignment
a Send Level control in the tree, after the assignment
the right inspector strip after the assignment
observations.note: the DESTINATION aux, not the sending strip

observations.what: send slots carrying the `Send slot.` help prefix, after the assignment
menu marks read after the assignment, on the slot the probe opens
observations.title: No Send

observations.what: menu marks read on the slot that OWNS the assignment — the `send button` immediately preceding the `send knob` — while the send existed
observations.title: No Send
observations.corroboration: at the same instant the tree read `send button send knob` and Logic's undo entry read `Undo Change Send in Channel Strip`

conclusion:
The send slot's menu marks its choice, and that mark does NOT report an assignment: with a send to `Bus 12` in place — corroborated at the same instant by the Send Level knob being present and by Logic's undo entry — the slot that owns it still marks the no-send entry. The checkmark is therefore CLOSED as a source-side readback for this ADR.

What did come back positive is smaller and real: a Send Level slider exists only once a send is assigned. Its presence reports that a slot holds a send — not which destination — so it answers the earlier record's open question about that control and gives the graph one source-side fact it did not have.
limits: The negative is about the MARK, not about the menu. The menu still offers 275 distinct destination titles and a selection still lands; nothing here weakens the write path.
`No Send` is this host's spelling. An implementation reading marks at all must go through AXLocalePolicy; the finding that the mark does not move is independent of the spelling.

One send, one strip, one project, one locale. The slot that owns the assignment was identified as the `send button` immediately preceding the `send knob`; that ordering was read from the tree in the same runs and is not an independently established rule.

Submenus were not opened. If Logic ever nested destinations, an unopened submenu's items are absent from the tree and a mark inside one would not have been seen — measured here, the 275 titles including `Bus 12` are top-level, so this does not affect the reading.
The probe moves the strip's Mute control as part of its protocol, so back-to-back invocations are not reading an unchanged strip.
